blocks.heading: Employer associations
blocks.text: An employers’ association is a group of employers joining together to provide benefits to its members. It can represent employer interests, share information, offer advice, support training (such as off-the-job courses for members’ staff, or guidance for on-the-job training) and contribute to bargaining or discussions affecting an industry. It is distinct from a trade union representing workers, although both may participate in industrial-relations discussions. Membership can pool expertise that one small employer cannot easily obtain alone; subscriptions and differing member interests can limit its appeal. An association does not become the employer of every member’s workers merely by providing advice.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Eno Metals joins a workshop-employers’ association to obtain advice on managing staffing changes and discuss shared industry concerns. The association supports employers, while the employees’ union represents workers. Advice may improve preparation but does not guarantee that every dispute will be resolved in the employer’s favour.
